steps.title: The fifth mini recital
steps.body:
Same shape as every recital, but each part is now a rehearsed plan: the first ten seconds, the slip plan, the bow. Nothing here should be a surprise to you, even if it is new to the audience.

1. Choose two pieces, one from this sprint and one older.
2. Run each once a day, starting with the exact first ten seconds you planned in week 7.
3. Say the slip plan out loud before you play: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar.
4. On recital day, walk up, sit, breathe, begin, exactly as rehearsed, then hold the last note and bow.
5. The family asks one question. Answer it, then write the Practice log.

A performance that feels calm is not luck. It is a plan you rehearsed enough times that it stopped feeling like a plan.

figure.alt: A bar of four beats ending in a held note, matching the checklist's own line: last note held, hands off, then a bow.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Two pieces chosen, one from this sprint and one older
Each piece run once a day, starting with the planned first ten seconds
Slip plan said out loud: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar
Last note held, hands off, then a bow
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, the first ten seconds included, phone where it sees the hands.
